title: org.prodid.entity
description: What the resolver answers for one entity. Every value a reader sees sits inside a claim that names the source that made it and when it was first seen; there are no bare fields.

parents.description: The entity's ancestors as opids: an item has a variant and a family, a variant has a family, a family has neither.

children.description: The opids one level down: a family's variants, a variant's items. Absent or empty for an item.

merged_from.description: Opids merged into this one. Each of them resolves here with 308.

claims.description: Active claims about this entity. With ?history=1 the withdrawn ones are included, each carrying withdrawn_at.

opid.description: Opaque index identifier, never parsed by a reader.

value.description: Normalized: a GTIN or a restricted circulation number is the 14-digit form, left-padded with zeros. Never blank or untrimmed.

scope.description: What the value is unique within. Required for mpn, sku and rcn, and present for nothing else: the normalized brand for mpn, the source's name for sku and rcn. Without it a restricted number would read as a global one.

gtinValue.description: The normalized 14-digit form. All zeros is a placeholder, not an identifier.

property.description: A built-in property, or a publisher key under variant. or properties. — the namespace that keeps a publisher's own `name` from colliding with the built-in one.

lang.description: BCP 47 tag. Carried only by claims whose value is text the publisher wrote: brand, name, variant.*, and those properties.* whose value is a string or a list of strings.

seen_at.description: When this source began asserting this value, and has not stopped since. It does not change while the claim keeps being asserted, and it is not when the fact was first published anywhere: a claim re-asserted after a withdrawal carries the later date.

withdrawn_at.description: When the source stopped asserting it. Present only on withdrawn claims, which are returned only with ?history=1.

text.description: What a lang tag can apply to: a string, or a list of strings.

mediaValue.description: The value of a media claim. The index stores the file under its digest; a reader fetches media_url, and url says where the source published it.

url.description: Where the source published the file.

media_url.description: Where the index serves the stored copy.

source.description: Who said it. The full status of a source is at /source/{name}.

lapsed.description: True while the source's discovery is failing. Its claims stay readable and stay marked.
